title: Stability: priority queueing and geo-aware degradation for similarity reranker
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: The similarity reranker experiences intermittent tail latency and request loss during global load spikes. Customers running multi-region workloads face uneven degradation; high-priority customers see throttling after best-effort tenants exhaust shared queues. Current mitigations (basic timeouts + single global circuit breaker) are brittle and cause cascading failures or overly aggressive drops.

Goal: Implement a layered stability architecture for the reranker that improves P99 latency, prevents slow cascades, and provides graceful quality degradation per-customer and per-region while preserving throughput for high-priority traffic. Deliverables: priority-based admission, token-weighted concurrency limits, hierarchical circuit breakers (per-model, per-region), geo-aware routing with local short-circuiting to approximate/k-NN fallback, and observability for runbooks and rollback.

Scope: server-side changes to reranker admission control, routing layer (smart-router), runtime configs for autoscaling, and Console dashboards + runbooks. Non-goals: offline model changes to ranking heuristics and embedding model retraining (except where used by graceful fallback to approximate embeddings).
acceptance_criteria: P99 inference latency reduced by 30% under 2x baseline traffic bursts for tiered customers (measured on benchmark harness)
High-priority customers retain >= 95% of successful responses when low-priority tenants saturate capacity in synthetic overload tests
Circuit breaker escalations logged and expose root cause (region/model/concurrency) in Console traces
Canary rollout plan defined and executed across two regions with automatic rollback on SLO breach
Comprehensive dashboards and alerts added: queue-depth-by-tenant, admission-rate, breaker-state, fallback-rate, approx-kNN-hitrate
implementation_notes: Benchmark harness used: benchmarks/rerank-stability/2026-02 (scripts in repo)
Autoscaler knobs: target_cpu 65%, custom metric request_queue_depth per-shard, staged scale window 45s -> 5m
risks_and_tradeoffs: Priority queuing increases head-of-line blocking risk for medium-priority when high-priority sustained; mitigated by token-weighted fairness (leaky-bucket per-priority)
Introducing local approximate-kNN fallbacks trades some relevance quality for latency guarantees; will be gated by per-customer config and verified via eval prompts
Per-region circuit breakers add operational complexity and noisy signals — invested in richer tracing and aggregation to avoid alert fatigue
Adding admission control at router increases request path complexity; aim to keep canonical fast-path for common non-throttled requests
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-weighted admission and breaker state transitions
Integration tests in staging with mixed-priority synthetic clients (10k qps mix), verify tail latency and success ratios
Chaos test: randomly flip region-level backbone connectivity to validate geo-degradation and fallback correctness
A/B experiment: 10% traffic to new admission path for 48 hours, measure client-facing errors and latency
Load test with retained-cold-cache and cached-fast-path scenarios to ensure cache-priming behaves as expected
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy admission + breaker config to staging; smoke tests
2) Canary in us-east-1 (5% traffic) for 24h, monitor SLOs and fallback rate
3) Expand canary to eu-west-1 (10% traffic) and run mixed-tenant stress tests
4) If stable, promote to 50% across both regions and validate autoscaler behavior
5) Full rollout with feature-flag off-by-default per-tenant; enable for early adopter customers first
notes: Oncall runbook updated: /runbooks/reranker-stability (include steps to disable admission throttling and revert router short-circuit)
